title: Measuring K for iron(III) thiocyanate with a spectrophotometer

stimulus.title: A colored equilibrium measured with Beer’s law
stimulus.html:
Iron(III) ions react with thiocyanate ions to form a red complex ion:

Fe3+(aq) + SCN−(aq) ⇌ FeSCN2+(aq)

FeSCN2+ is the only colored species at the wavelength used. A student mixes 5.00 mL of 2.00 × 10−3 M Fe(NO3)3 with 5.00 mL of 2.00 × 10−3 M KSCN at 25 °C, waits for the color to stop changing, and measures the absorbance in a 1.00 cm cuvette. From a calibration curve, the molar absorptivity of FeSCN2+ at this wavelength is 4.50 × 103 M−1 cm−1.

Data
QuantityValue
Volume of 2.00 × 10−3 M Fe(NO3)35.00 mL
Volume of 2.00 × 10−3 M KSCN5.00 mL
Absorbance of the equilibrium mixture0.297

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant, Kc, for the reaction.

rubric.point: Correct K<sub>c</sub> expression, products over reactants, with no water or spectator ions.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: (i) Calculate the concentration of Fe3+ in the mixture immediately after mixing, before any reaction. (ii) Calculate [FeSCN2+] in the equilibrium mixture.

rubric.point: (i) Uses the total volume (10.00 mL) for the dilution: 1.00 × 10⁻³ M.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Calculate the value of Kc at 25 °C. Show how you found each equilibrium concentration.

rubric.point: Equilibrium [Fe³⁺] = [SCN⁻] = 1.00 × 10⁻³ − 6.60 × 10<sup>−5</sup> = 9.34 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M (an ICE table or equivalent reasoning).
accept: ICE table with change −x, −x, +x and x = [FeSCN²⁺]
value consistent with the student’s part (b) answers

parts.sample: Initial: [Fe<sup>3+</sup>] = [SCN<sup>−</sup>] = 1.00 × 10<sup>−3</sup> M, [FeSCN<sup>2+</sup>] = 0. Change: −x, −x, +x, with x = 6.60 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M. Equilibrium: [Fe<sup>3+</sup>] = [SCN<sup>−</sup>] = 9.34 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M. K<sub>c</sub> = (6.60 × 10<sup>−5</sup>) / (9.34 × 10<sup>−4</sup>)<sup>2</sup> = 75.7.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Identify the piece of glassware the student should use to measure each 5.00 mL volume, and justify your choice.

rubric.point: A 5.00 mL volumetric pipet (or a buret), because it delivers the volume to three significant figures; a graduated cylinder is too imprecise.

parts.sample: A 5.00 mL volumetric pipet, because it delivers exactly 5.00 mL (to ±0.01 mL), matching the precision of the data; a graduated cylinder is not precise enough.

parts.label: e
parts.prompt: A few drops of concentrated Fe(NO3)3 solution are added to the equilibrium mixture at 25 °C. (i) Predict whether the absorbance will increase, decrease or stay the same once equilibrium is re-established. (ii) Justify your prediction in terms of Q and K.

rubric.point: (ii) Adding Fe³⁺ increases the denominator, so Q < K; the net reaction proceeds forward, forming more FeSCN²⁺ (the colored species) until Q = K.
accept: Q decreases below K, so net forward
reasoning must use Q compared with K; "K increases" or rate language alone earns no point

parts.sample: (i) The absorbance increases. (ii) Adding Fe<sup>3+</sup> makes Q = [FeSCN<sup>2+</sup>] / ([Fe<sup>3+</sup>][SCN<sup>−</sup>]) smaller than K, because the denominator increases. With Q < K, the net reaction proceeds forward, forming more FeSCN<sup>2+</sup>, until Q = K. More FeSCN<sup>2+</sup> means a higher absorbance.

parts.label: f
parts.prompt: (i) A classmate says, "Kc is greater than 1, so the equilibrium mixture contains more FeSCN2+ than Fe3+." Use your results to evaluate the claim. (ii) When the equilibrium mixture is warmed to 40 °C, its absorbance decreases. Determine whether the forward reaction is exothermic or endothermic, and justify your answer.

rubric.point: (i) The claim is wrong: [FeSCN²⁺] = 6.6 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M is far less than [Fe³⁺] = 9.3 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M. K > 1 here because the denominator is the product of two small concentrations, so K > 1 does not mean products exceed each reactant.
accept: cites the two concentrations and rejects the claim
explains that K compares products to the product of reactant concentrations

rubric.point: (ii) Exothermic: lower absorbance means less FeSCN²⁺ at the higher temperature, so K decreased as T increased, which is true of an exothermic forward reaction.
accept: heating shifts the equilibrium toward reactants, so heat is a product: exothermic
K decreases with temperature, so ΔH < 0

parts.sample: (i) The claim is incorrect. At equilibrium [FeSCN<sup>2+</sup>] = 6.6 × 10<sup>−5</sup> M while [Fe<sup>3+</sup>] = 9.3 × 10<sup>−4</sup> M, about 14 times larger. K<sub>c</sub> is greater than 1 only because the denominator is the product of two small concentrations. (ii) Exothermic. A lower absorbance means less FeSCN<sup>2+</sup>, so the equilibrium shifted toward the reactants when heated. That means K decreased as the temperature rose, which happens when the forward reaction releases heat (ΔH < 0).
